The Great Downzoning of American cities is a complete suite of policies — rent control is meant to protect incumbent tenants from the downside of barring new construction, but then you need rules (like TOPA in DC) to discourage condo conversions.

A quirk of American life is that most of the people who sincerely enjoy urban living also have progressive ideological commitments that make them skeptical of pro-business politics, but those urban landscapes are the physical manifestation of large-scale capital investment.

We need to channel the progressive instinct into the fact that the pro-growth city will have more fiscal capacity to help poor families with their health care needs, will be more able to maintain mass transit, can open new schools & libraries.
